target_customer: Consumers in India (later the US) with obesity, Type 2 diabetes or other lifestyle conditions, paying for a coached program
problem: People struggle to lose weight and manage chronic lifestyle disease without sustained coaching, which is expensive and hard to access in India.
business_model: B2C subscription for a coached digital therapeutics program after a one-week free trial
product_category: Digital therapeutics for weight loss and diabetes reversal

founders.name: Rohan Verma
founders.background_notes: Inc42 says he and Aditya Kaicker were former ClassHop founders. Education and employers not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Aditya Kaicker
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page.

exit.reason: Not stated by the company. Reports describe layoffs in 2022 and a pullback from non-US markets.

technical_complexity.rationale: A coaching app with tracking and content, plus operations to run coaches at scale. No hard technical problem.

defensibility.rationale: Coaching programs and content could be copied by Indian digital health rivals; the main asset was coach operations and outcome data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it. Layoffs in 2022 and a US refocus followed.

market_need_then: India has a very large diabetes and obesity population and low access to coaching. The company claimed its program was three times as effective at a quarter of the cost.

branding.domain_note: Operated on breathewellbeing.in rather than a .com; US entity listed as Prana Health Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical and outcome focused marketing around diabetes reversal

branding.community_and_virality: The program included an online community; no evidence found of memes or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press about the brand itself, no logo or name story. The name is generic wellness wording shared with many firms.

outcome_analysis: Breathe Well-being raised about 6.5 million dollars in 2021 on a pitch of low cost coaching in India, then Inc42 reported in June 2022 that it cut about 50 staff because it was losing money and could not close a new round. Later reports describe about 90 to 100 more layoffs, a stop on onboarding outside the US, and pricing in India hurting profitability. A single outlet said the India business would wind down within six months. The company website still showed a 2023 copyright and a later pre-Series B of about 6 million dollars was reported by one outlet.
notes: The pre-Series B of about Rs 50 crore rests on a single outlet (The Startup Lab, listed in search, page not retrievable) and has no date; CB Insights and others report totals of about 12.8 to 12.9 million dollars. YC status Inactive while the website still appeared live with a 2023 footer. Competition list left empty: competitor names found (Fitterfly, Twin Health, Liva) came only from aggregator profiles with no dates near the batch. Pre-seed round label is my mapping of the source's 'pre-Series A'.
